ledger.note: 861: Ya'qub ibn al-Layth overthrows Dirham and makes himself emir of Sistan. 'In 861, Ya'qub overthrew Dirham, and gave himself the title of Emir at that point'; Saffarid infobox 'Established: 861', 'Capital: Zaranj'.

ledger.counterpart: Salih (ruler of Bost) and the ruler of ar-Rukkaj and Zamindawar
ledger.note: 864: Ya'qub marches on Bost and the Helmand lands. 'Yaʿqub led an expedition to Bost against his former master Salih' and 'ar-Rukkaj and Zamindāvar against the local ruler there'; the page says expedition, not annexation.

By 865: the Zunbils are beaten (the Zunbils dossier dates the loss to 866, the first year of the Cliopatria shape). The Saffarid page: Ya'qub's conquests included 'vanquishing the Zunbils and the Hindu Shahis by 865'; the Ya'qub page dates the capture of Kabul itself to 870, so only the Zunbil country (Zabulistan) is drawn here.
870: Ya'qub takes Kabul. 'Ya'qub defeated Kabul in 870 and again had to march there in 872'; the Saffarid page adds coins 'issued around 870 CE in Kabul on the Hindu Shahi model'.
870: Herat falls to the Saffarids. 'The Tahirid city of Herat was captured in 870'; the Ya'qub page has him marching on 'the Kharijites of Herat' in 870/871.

region.text: Khorasan around Nishapur, Herat excluded (taken in 870)

ledger.note: 870: the Saffarid-Tahirid war for Khorasan begins with the capture of Herat. 'The Tahirid city of Herat was captured in 870'; the fighting ends with the fall of Nishapur in 873.

871: Bamiyan captured. 'Bamiyan was captured in 871' (Tarikh-e-Sistan); Gardizi has an expedition of 870 that 'advanced as far as Kabul and Bamiyan'. The page says his army marched to 'Ghazna, Kabul, and Bamyan, conquering these territories from the Hindu Shahi'; the turk-shahis dossier ends in 870 and hindu-shahis starts in 870 (counterpart corrected by the me-08-b reviewer).

region.text: Khorasan around Nishapur, Herat excluded (taken in 870)

ledger.note: 873: the war ends when Ya'qub ousts the Tahirids from Nishapur.

region.text: Khorasan around Nishapur, Herat excluded (taken in 870)

ledger.note: 873: the Tahirids fall and Khorasan is annexed. 'In 873, Ya'qub ousted the Tahirids from their own capital of Nishapur'; Saffarid page 'overthrew the Tahirid dynasty, annexing Khorasan in 873'. The Ya'qub page also says 'by 870 AD the whole of Khorasan was brought under their control'; the 873 date is the one used.

874: Ya'qub invades Tabaristan. The Hasan ibn Zayd page: 'Ya'qub invaded Tabaristan and defeated the Zaydid forces at Sari', forcing Hasan 'once again to flee to the mountains of Daylam'; the Ya'qub page has only 'Ya'qub later traveled to Tabaristan in 874'.
874: the Saffarid army, hurt by heavy rain and disease, withdraws shortly after; no Saffarid garrison is recorded and Tabaristan stays Zaydi.

By 875 (page undated): Kerman. Saffarid page: 'Ya'qub then turned his focus to the west and began attacks on Khorasan, Khuzestan, Kerman (Southeastern Iran) and Fars (southwestern Iran)'; the caliphate was forced 'to recognize Ya'qub as governor of Sistan, Fars and Kerman'; 'By the time of Ya'qub's death, he had conquered ... Kerman, Fars'. The page dates none of these conquests; 875 is the year of Cliopatria's keyframe saffarid-dynasty_875, which already draws the land, so the ledger now carries it from the keyframe's first year (fx-24, snap F065, 1 Nov 2026).

The Ya'qub page's lead adds 'portions of western Pakistan'. The page dates none of these conquests; 875 is the year of Cliopatria's keyframe saffarid-dynasty_875, which already draws the land, so the ledger now carries it from the keyframe's first year (fx-24, snap F065, 1 Nov 2026).

region.text: the rest of the Saffarid shape of 875 that the caliphate held (Abbasid ledger 35's region): Sistan and Baluchestan, Baluchistan, Yazd, Hormozgan, the Esfahan edge and the Khuzestan edge, without Fars (the August 875 event) and Kerman (the event above)

ledger.note: By 875 (page undated): the rest of the Saffarid shape that the caliphate held. Saffarid page: the caliphate was forced 'to recognize Ya'qub as governor of Sistan, Fars and Kerman' (no year); 'The Saffarids then seized Khuzestan' (no year); 'By the time of Ya'qub's death, he had conquered the Kabul Valley, Tocharistan, Makran (Balochistan), Kerman, Fars' (879). The Ya'qub page dates only Fars (August 875) and his passage through Khuzistan before Wasit (24 March 876). Yazd, Hormozgan and the Esfahan edge are on no page opened: they are drawn only because Cliopatria's Saffarid row of 875 and this dossier's keyframe saffarid-dynasty_875 hold them. Without this gain the compiler skipped abbasid-caliphate ledger 35 (it is paired with the Persis and Kerman gains, whatever their region) and the Abbasids kept about 3,300 cells until the keyframe snap of 875 (fx-37, handoff H01 from fx-01, snap F072).

August 875: Ya'qub wins Fars at Lake Bakhtegan. 'They met near Lake Bakhtegan in August 875'; afterwards 'Ya'qub looted Muhammad's stronghold at Sa'idabad and took control of Fars'. The Saffarid page adds that the caliphate was forced 'to recognize Ya'qub as governor of Sistan, Fars and Kerman' (no year). The page names the defeated man only as Muhammad; the caliphate is the counterpart as the province's suzerain.

region.text: the lower Tigris from Baghdad to Wasit

ledger.note: March 876: Ya'qub marches on Baghdad. The caliph 'left Samarra' on 7 March 876, reached Baghdad on 15 March and Ya'qub 'entered Wasit on 24 March'.

region.text: the lower Tigris from Baghdad to Wasit

ledger.note: 8 April 876: the Saffarids are turned back at Dayr al-Aqul. 'The Battle of Dayr al-Aqul took place on 8 April 876' (the footnote: 'variously in the Arabic sources, such as 1 April'); the Saffarid page says the Abbasid army 'was able to turn them back'. Al-Muwaffaq had offered 'governorship of Khurasan, Tabaristan, Fars, Gurgan, and Ray' and Ya'qub refused.

region.text: Kabul and the country down to Lamghan, recaptured by Lalliya

ledger.note: 878: Lalliya retakes Kabul. Hindu Shahis page: 'The region was in Saffarid control until 878 CE before being recaptured by Lalliya, the successor to Samanta'. Mirror of hindu-shahis ledger 1 (gain 878); added by fx-24 (1 Nov 2026, conflict F148) because the keyframes of 878-899 still drew the Kabul valley as Saffarid. The page also puts a Saffarid governor of Kabul, Khudrayaka, in office to 880 and has Kabul 'reverting back as Shahi territory' only when next mentioned in 900; 878 follows the page's 'until 878 CE'.

897: the caliph hands Ray to the Saffarids. The Amr page says Ray was handed to the Saffarids in 897 (and that the caliph named Amr governor of Transoxiana in 898, an investiture only); its later loss is not described. Ray was lost to the Samanids in 901.

region.text: Balkh and Bactria, the Oxus frontier

ledger.note: Spring 900: Amr and Isma'il Samani meet at Balkh. 'In the spring of 900, Amr clashed with Ismail near Balkh, but was defeated and taken into captivity'; the caliph al-Mu'tadid had 'named Amr ibn al-Layth governor of Transoxiana in 898' and had urged Isma'il to fight him.

region.text: Khorasan, Bactria and the Saffarid east

ledger.note: 900: Khorasan passes to the Samanids. 'Amr was crushingly defeated and taken prisoner in 900' (Amr page); 'Ismail was thereafter recognized as the ruler of all of Khorasan and Transoxiana by the caliph' (Samanid page) and the caliph 'invested Ismail with Khorasan' (Isma'il page); 'Amr bin Laith was forced to surrender most of his territories' (Saffarid page).

region.text: Balkh and Bactria, the Oxus frontier

ledger.note: 900: the Balkh campaign ends with Amr in captivity. 'The two sides fought in Balkh, northern Afghanistan during the spring of 900', after which 'Amr was captured, and some of his troops switched sides'; Amr was sent to Baghdad and executed in April 902.

901: Ray falls to the Samanids. The Isma'il page has the Samanid army sent 'into northern Persia in 901' that 'managed to conquer several other cities including Ray'; the caliph invested Isma'il 'with Khorasan, Tabaristan, Ray, and Isfahan'.
910: the Abbasids recover Fars. 'It was not until 910 that the Abbasids managed to regain the coveted Fars province.'

911: Sistan falls under Samanid control. 'by 911, Sistan was under complete Samanid control'; the Saffarid page says 'In 912, the Samanids finally expelled the Saffarids from Sistan' and that a civil war between Tahir and the pretender al-Layth ibn Ali had broken out in Sistan in 908. Kerman, held in the 900s, is not mentioned again.

922: the Saffarid line returns to Sistan. The Saffarid page: Sistan 'became independent again under the Saffarid Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Muhammad' (undated in the text), and its table dates Ahmad 922-963. The Nasr II page says 'The Abbasids managed to recover Sistan for the last time' without a year, so the counterpart may be the caliphate rather than the Samanids; Cliopatria draws the Samanids over Sistan to 999.
November 1002: Mahmud of Ghazni invades Sistan in person. 'Mahmud decided to come personally in November 1002'; he had already 'led his troops into Sistan in 1000'.
December 1002: Khalaf surrenders. 'By December 1002 Khalaf was forced to surrender.'

1002: Sistan passes to the Ghaznavids. 'In 1002, Mahmud of Ghazni invaded Sistan, dethroned Khalaf ibn Ahmad and finally ended the Saffarid dynasty.' The Khalaf page has Ghaznavid rule of Sistan 'until 1029'.
1002: the Saffarid dynasty ends with Khalaf's deposition by Mahmud of Ghazni (surrender by December; he died in 1009 at Gardez).

wars.name: Saffarid conquest of Khorasan
wars.outcome: Saffarid victory: Herat taken in 870, Nishapur and the Tahirids ousted in 873, Khorasan annexed.

wars.name: Saffarid campaign against Tabaristan
wars.outcome: Victory at Sari over the Zaydid forces, then withdrawal; no territory kept.
wars.note: The Ya'qub page says only 'Ya'qub later traveled to Tabaristan in 874'; the Saffarid page names the 'Zaydis of Tabaristan' among unorthodox groups. Cliopatria draws the Alid state apart from the Saffarids throughout.

wars.name: Saffarid–Abbasid war of 875–876

zones.text: the Tigris from Baghdad to Wasit

wars.outcome: Fars won in August 875; the march on Baghdad was turned back at Dayr al-Aqul on 8 April 876.
wars.note: Includes the Battle of Dayr al-Aqul.

wars.name: Saffarid–Samanid war of 898–900
wars.outcome: Samanid victory at Balkh in spring 900; Amr captured (executed 902); Khorasan to Isma'il.
wars.note: Samanid page and Ismail page give 900; the Saffarid page's later text says 901.

wars.name: Samanid conquest of Saffarid Sistan
wars.outcome: Samanid control of Sistan by 911; the Saffarids 'expelled' in 912.
wars.note: Civil war of 908 between Tahir and the pretender al-Layth ibn Ali; the page gives 908 and 912 for different steps.

wars.name: Samanid-backed campaign against Khalaf
wars.outcome: Khalaf 'gave battle but was defeated in August of 979'; no territorial change recorded on the page.
wars.note: Khalaf had neglected the customary tribute to Bukhara.

wars.name: Saffarid raid on Buyid Kerman
wars.outcome: Tahir invaded Kerman 'in 1000' without lasting gains.

wars.name: Ghaznavid conquest of Sistan
wars.outcome: Mahmud entered Sistan in 1000 and took it in person in November-December 1002; Khalaf surrendered by December.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier appears on any page opened; the Saffarid east and west edges are approximate, and Sistan itself is the only core with fixed seats (Zaranj, Taq).

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Saffarid Dynasty' ends 899 and gives its whole shape to the Samanids from 900; the dynasty continued: Fars and Kerman to 910, Sistan to 911/912, and after a gap (912-921, no Saffarid ruler on any page opened) a Sistan emirate 922-1002 that paid tribute to Bukhara. This dossier therefore runs 861-1002 with new keyframes for 864, 873, 900, 910 and 922 and shows Cliopatria's 898-899 shapes as wrong (they reach Bukhara on the strength of a caliphal grant). The Saffarid infobox has no area, so no area comparison could be made. Pages disagree on the Balkh year (900 on the Samanid, Isma'il and Amr pages; 901 once on the Samanid page), on Amr's reign end (900/901/902), on Ya'qub's start (861 vs 867 in his own table), on Khorasan (873 vs 'by 870'), and on the end of Saffarid Sistan (911 Samanid page vs 912 Saffarid page). Dossiers needed from other groups: tahirid-dynasty (Khorasan and Herat to 873; Cliopatria lacks it) and zunbils (Zabulistan; Cliopatria lacks it); kharijite Salih of Bost is not a state. The Banu Khalaf and the Saffarid line after 1002 are out of scope. Region names the gazetteer lacks: none (Sistan, Persis, Khorasan, Bactria, Zabulistan, Kabulistan are all listed). Not opened (page budget 5; four used for the Saffarids alone): Tahirid dynasty, Zunbils, Battle of Dayr al-Aqul, Battle of Balkh (900).
R039 (3 Nov 2026): abbasid-caliphate removed from identity.successors. The handover schema has no date, so the entry made rule R2 give the Abbasids every Saffarid/Abbasid conflict cell from 750 on, for the Saffarid's whole life. The Saffarid page's infobox lists the Samanid Empire and the Ghaznavid Empire as successors and the Abbasid Caliphate only as a predecessor ('Preceded by: Tahirid dynasty; Abbasid Caliphate; Zunbil dynasty'); the return of Fars to the caliphate (910) is carried by ledger/24 (loss, counterpart abbasid-caliphate); the page: 'Under Tahir ibn Muhammad ibn Amr (901-908), the dynasty fought the Abbasids for the possession of Fars.' The removed entry read: land Persis ('Fars, not until 910 that the Abbasids managed to regain the coveted Fars province'), note 'Fars passed back to the caliphate in 910.'
